scope: R1/DL-VERIFY-01 checksum-file mismatch semantics, offline-cache downgrade coverage, and IMP-08 configuration path injection guard
status: implemented-and-isolated-verified; live download and live manager configuration not performed
implementation: parse_sha256_checksum_file now distinguishes 'the file listed other assets' from 'the file has no usable entries'
a valid checksum file that lists N other assets reports that count and warns the version or asset name may have changed
the empty/unparseable case keeps its original shorter message so the two conditions stay distinguishable
validate_tool_config_layout rejects configuration paths containing semicolon, quote, NUL, CR or LF
the rejection is explicit: the value is also written into manager configuration files, where such characters would change the file's meaning

no dead code was added: the speculative AssetFingerprint/cached_verification_for_asset draft was removed after confirming resolve_download_spec re-fetches and re-parses the checksum file on every install and never reuses a cached digest

reviewFindings.checksumMismatch: covered: parser rejects missing entries, malformed digests, conflicting digests, path traversal in the target name, and now other-asset listings
reviewFindings.assetReplacement: covered by design and now by a fixture: offline cache rows are downgraded to Unverified, and resolve_download_spec always re-fetches the checksum file, so a replaced asset cannot inherit an old trusted digest

No live package-manager configuration was written with a rejected path
Official checksum sources for the remaining 16 tools are still pending R0 review
limitations: The path guard is character-based; it does not attempt to escape values for every manager's config syntax
A checksum file that lists the target plus other assets is still accepted, which is correct, but the extra entries are not reported
Asset replacement detection relies on the publisher changing the checksum file; a silently swapped asset with an unchanged checksum entry remains undetectable by design
